newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Ruehe confident on Eurofighter.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Ruehe confident on Eurofighter.

text.p: Defence Minister Volker Ruehe said he was confident Germany would raise the necessary funds to pay for the Eurofighter project, but said he was not sure about the financing for a German-French spy satellite programme.

Speaking to a group of foreign journalists on Tuesday evening, Ruehe also said the eagerness of central and eastern European nations to join NATO proved the alliance was now as important a stability anchor for Europe as it has ever been.
"The Eurofighter will come," Ruehe said. "We have worked hard for the last four years and now we have to get the money."

Finance Minister Theo Waigel, struggling to close budget holes, had said on Tuesday he believed Germany should buy the four-country combat jet. Germany would take 180 Eurofighters for about 23 billion marks ($13.3 billion).

Germany's Eurofighter partners are fretting at the delay to a firm order by Bonn. Eurofighter's partners include DASA, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG, British Aerospace Plc, Alenia of Italy and state-owned CASA of Spain.

Ruehe, when asked about the proposed French-German satellite programmes Helios and Horus, said there would be further talks about the project later this year. But he said there was no funding available for the project at the moment.
Ahead of next month's NATO summit in Madrid, Ruehe said even though there was no immediate threat to security in Europe at the moment, there was no doubt that NATO was still needed.

"NATO is the greatest stability anchor," Ruehe said. "If it were irrelevant, why are all its members staying? And why are 11 or 12 nations standing in line to get in? I think that shows that NATO plays a very relevant role."

Turning to domestic political issues, Ruehe said he was confident his ruling Christian Democratic (CDU) party would pull out of its current slump in the opinion polls before the next general elections in September 1998.

"I believe our strategy is right," Ruehe said. "The government is talking about the need for reform and change whereas the opposition and unions are talking about trying to continue the same system we have now."

Asked whether he was "tempted" to someday become chancellor, Ruehe said: "I have always taken it as compliment for my work whenever my name is mentioned. It is delightful in that it makes my job (as defence minister) easier. But beyond that, I have not made any thoughts about it." ($ = 1.725 German Marks)
